newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes likely to rise with arbitrage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes likely to rise with arbitrage.

text.p: U.S. foreign crudes are likely to rise near-term into the U.S. Gulf due to a more profitable arbitrage, helped by an overhang of prompt North Sea cargoes, traders said on Wednesday.
U.S. refiners covering prompt requirements, however, may still find domestic grades more competitive.
"The arbitrage is open but we have to consider that runs will be cut for Fall turnarounds," an East Coast trader said, estimating runs could drop 500,000 barrels per day (bpd).
In late U.S. trade, Brent sold near the weaker end of its recent range at Oct Brent minus 43.5 cents fob.
Evidence of a wider arbitrage was seen in more Atlantic and West African fixtures, traders said.
Apart from a U.S. trader's Brent charter, a U.K. refiner was also seen having fixed a 140,000 tonne vessel loading Sept 29 from Sullom Voe to the U.S. Gulf.
Sellers were not seen offering Brent to the U.S., although cargoes were thought available for mid-Oct arrival.
Norwegian grades such as Oseberg was assessed around WTI minus 5-10 cents cif, for mid-Oct.
A cargo of Qua Iboe was rumored sold earlier this week at WTI plus 40 cents cif.
Within the region, a major reportedly sold Cano Limon for Oct 6-12 at WTI minus $1.55 fob on Wednesday, while two mid-Oct Cusianas were heard offered around WTI parity fob.
In the paper market, Brent outright Nov Brent partials traded between $22.30-26, a notch below the IPE close.
And Oct/Nov Brent traded near the day's high at 55 cents.
